title: Micro-sprint runbook to operationalize prefetch/batching/quantization guardrails
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a pragmatic, ops-friendly runbook and sprint cadence for delivering targeted unit-economy savings via three levers: dynamic batching, request prefetch/KV-ttl strategies, and conservative quantization profiles. Goal: enable product teams to run short (1-2 week) experiments with clear safety gates, automated rollback hooks, and standardized evaluation so we can capture repeatable savings without quality regressions. Scope includes: templates for canary rollouts, standardized eval prompts and pass thresholds, monitoring dashboards with token-cost delta and P95 latency, and an operator checklist for manual overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook draft published in Confluence with step-by-step canary + rollback flow
Two pilot micro-sprints completed (one batching-prefetch, one quantization) with documented before/after cost and quality metrics
Automated regression gate implemented: evaluation harness that returns a pass/fail for prompt-suite with configurable thresholds
One-click rollback and routing policy created in Console for canary traffic splits
Post-mortem template and cost-impact dashboard tile added to central observability
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff with Eng (runtime, infra), DX, and SRE. Aligned on micro-sprint format (10 working days) and success metrics: token-savings %, P95 latency delta, user-visible failure rate.

2026-02-28: Drafted evaluation prompt-suite (50 prompts across high/med/low context). Decision: require >=98% semantic preservation score and <5% increase in hallucination rate to proceed with quantization canary.

2026-03-03: Engineering spike demonstrated 12-18% token cost reduction when combining 1) prefix prefetch TTL ladder and 2) 2x batching window on background inference. Noted 90ms P95 latency increase — agreed to adjust batching window heuristics.

2026-03-07: Design and Console teams provided canary UI wireframes. Added explicit 'safety threshold' input and automated alerting to Ops channel. Action: PM to finalize runbook checklist and link SLOs.
2026-03-10: Held pre-pilot readiness review. Blocking: regression harness needs integration with CI. Plan: ENG-49821 to add harness by 2026-03-17, then kick pilot on 2026-03-22.
outcomes: Establish reproducible micro-sprint pattern for econ experiments
Reduce token-unit cost on piloted workloads by 10-20% without user-visible quality regressions
Create standardized artifacts to accelerate team-led cost pilots (runbook, eval-suite, dashboard templates)
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive batching saves cost but increases tail latency; we will advertise batch knobs with tiered targets per route (interactive vs async).
Decision: quantization will be opt-in per model with a conservative default (8-bit dynamic) and rollback if eval fails. Quant profiles documented in Confluence.
Follow-ups: add automated A/B comparison of semantic similarity using embedding distance in the eval harness; experiment with TTL ladder heuristics to avoid cache thrash.
